text:
Maya (CS): Hey team, customer ACME reported that when they remove users from an Okta group that is mapped to an internal role the users sometimes keep access for ~24h. They see deprovisioning events in Okta but Redwood doesn't drop the role. Can someone help triage?

Sam (SRE): Thanks Maya. Do we have the customer org id and an example user?

Maya (CS): Org: acme-corp. Example user: jessica@acme.com. They say the Okta event shows a group membership change (remove) and SCIM PATCH was sent with membership delta.

Maya (CS): They included the raw payload from Okta: 
```json
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    {
      "op": "Replace",
      "path": "members",
      "value": []
    }
  ]
}
```

Jen (Identity Eng): Hmm. Is ACME using delegated SCIM connector (Okta -> our SCIM) or our builtin provisioning?

Maya (CS): Delegated connector (Okta -> Redwood SCIM). They also said group externalId changed recently (renamed in Okta and externalId got normalized).

Sam (SRE): Can you paste the audit log id from our side for the incoming SCIM request? I want to see how our provisioner handled the externalId.

Maya (CS): Sure — provisioner-bot logged request id p-0a1b2c3d and status 200 from our API gateway. Raw body attached in the ticket.

provisioner-bot: Received PATCH /Groups/{groupId} id=p-0a1b2c3d src=okta org=acme-corp status=200

Jen (Identity Eng): I pulled p-0a1b2c3d. The incoming group object had externalId "ACME::eng-all" but in our DB we still store it as "acme:eng-all" (lowercased, single colon) — upstream rename introduced double-colon and caps. Our group-to-role mapper is currently exact-match on externalId. That would explain why members were never reconciled out of the role.

Liam (DevEx): Oof. So this is an externalId normalization mismatch. Do we normalize on write or on match?

Jen (Identity Eng): Currently we normalize on write for new groups, but we did a schema migration last quarter and a handful of migrated groups kept legacy normalized keys. We missed a backfill for delegated connectors.

Sam (SRE): That aligns: gateway returned 200 for PATCH (we acked) but our membershipSync job only reconciles if group externalId matches mapping. Since externalId changed, the membership delta was applied to an effective group that doesn't map to the role anchor.

Maya (CS): Customer reports some users lost access (the ones in groups we did match) but a subset remained, so it fits. What is the mitigation we can give them now?

Jen (Identity Eng): Short term: run a manual group backfill that re-normalizes externalIds for delegated connector groups and then run membershipSync for affected groups. I can run a one-off script if you give me list of affected groupIds.

Maya (CS): I'll request group ids from ACME and escalate. They gave one example group id: 0g9k8l7m.

Jen (Identity Eng): Ok. For that group I can run: 
```bash
python tools/migrate_group_externalid.py --org acme-corp --group 0g9k8l7m --normalize
# then trigger membership sync
python tools/run_membership_sync.py --group 0g9k8l7m
```

Sam (SRE): Also question — are token scopes for the delegated connector adequate? If Okta is sending PATCH and we accept 200, our connector should be able to PATCH membership. But if connector uses limited scope (read-only groups) some changes might be ignored by our business logic. Any evidence?

Maya (CS): Okta audit shows the connector used the "scim.edit" scope. No errors returned.

Jen (Identity Eng): Scope looks fine. Root cause still is mismatch on externalId normalization + migrated groups skipped during backfill. We'll run the manual fix.

provisioner-bot: Action queued: normalize_externalid p-0a1b2c3d -> task t-77f.

Liam (DevEx): FYI we should add a resilient matching rule: if no exact externalId match, try case-insensitive and delimiter-agnostic match (treat single vs double colon as equivalent) and log a warning. That would prevent regressions for renamed groups.

Jen (Identity Eng): Agreed. I'll file an RFC for matching improvements and add a migration to backfill the rest of delegated connector groups. Short term patch: best-effort match on normalized key for 7 days.

Sam (SRE): For postmortem we should include: incident timeline, affected users count (CS to provide), workaround performed, and longer-term fix ETA.

Maya (CS): ACME says ~42 users retained access incorrectly. They want confirmation when fixed. I told them we'd schedule the backfill and let them know ETA.

Jen (Identity Eng): I'll run the normalize + membershipSync within the hour for the example group and report back. If that clears the user jessica@acme.com we'll mark this resolved.

Jen (Identity Eng): Update: ran normalize and sync for 0g9k8l7m. Membership delta applied; jessica@acme.com lost the role as expected. Verified via admin UI and audit events: 
```text
provisioner: removed role "eng-read" from user jessica@acme.com userId=usr-555 time=2026-03-15T14:12:03Z
```

Maya (CS): Customer confirmed via Slack that access removed. They asked if we can avoid this in future.

Jen (Identity Eng): Next steps: 1) emergency backfill for delegated connector groups (ETA 48h) 2) change matching to be tolerant (PR next week) 3) add monitoring alert when SCIM externalId mismatch rate spikes. I'll open tickets and assign owners.

Liam (DevEx): I'll add a note to the onboarding docs for delegated connectors reminding about normalization caveats.

Maya (CS): Great — I'll update the ACME ticket with the workaround and our roadmap items. Marking this thread for follow-up after the backfill. :white_check_mark:

okta-bot: Okta event: group.0g9k8l7m.membership.change processed -> acked by Redwood (p-0a1b2c3d)

Sam (SRE): Leaving this open until backfill completes. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
